_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: COBI has a dark mode, and one control drives it. The Theme selector in the header (System · Light · Dark) sets every tab and follows you into a second window; before this there were genuinely FOUR different answers to "is it dark" hiding behind what looked like one setting misbehaving. Measured across all 38 tabs, dark went from every route failing accessibility to 26, and light improved too (19 → 17) rather than regressing. SkyView got Sam's five: a slower turn, a course that stays where you drop it instead of snapping back, courses grouped by level where we have the indicator (only 12% of them do), CTE-vs-academic checkboxes, and an Isolate toggle. There is now a standing procedure for this kind of work — /a11y-pass — because the reports were being read in the wrong order: a sweep of 511 findings was really six problems repeated on every tab. The glyph sweep it comes with is built and tested but NOT run: it would rewrite 516 button and link labels across 139 files, and that needs Sam's go first.

items.text: Eleven pending decisions are on one sheet with reply chips — three from this session (the glyph run, whether the three approved emoji exceptions are in scope, how SkyView should follow the header's Theme control), five carried from Session 244 that have never been answered, and three that are not decisions at all but want your eye on something already shipped. Reply on the sheet and the session reads it back: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a6821715-4c49-43f1-be7a-b2a7a8f3b487

Go / no-go on the glyph clean-up. You asked to remove all emoji glyphs and replace the crucial ones with a muted mark in white and CO blue. The tool is built and tested; running it rewrites 516 button and link labels across 139 files in one pass. It is deliberately not run yet — say go and it happens with the full test suite and both accessibility sweeps after it. (item on the decision sheet — reply there.)

One reading to confirm: "remove all emoji glyphs" was taken to include the three we had previously approved and protected — the To-Do button, the guidance pane and the Governance tab. They are now in scope as muted CO-blue marks. If you meant to keep those three as they are, say so and the carve-out goes back. (item on the decision sheet — reply there.)

SkyView follows the header's Theme control only as a fallback: your own SkyView choice still wins, and "Night by default" still owns the default when nobody has chosen. That layering was a judgment call — worth your eye, and easy to change. (item on the decision sheet — reply there.)

The largest remaining source of dark-mode faults is mechanical: about 140 places still pair a themed blue fill with a hard-coded white text color, which reads at 2.65:1 wherever a pane paints one. The --on-accent token exists and is already applied to the two that appeared on every tab.

Some cards and table cells hard-code a white background, so they stay light islands when the page goes dark. The Workplan Goals cells are the worked example and they are written by the daily generator — so the fix belongs in excel_to_dashboard.py, never in the HTML, which the next cron would overwrite.

The SkyView lane file is two and a half times its size budget and the docs lint says so every run. It is invariants rather than stacked history, so compacting it means reading and ruling on each one — several predate decisions that superseded them. Worth its own sitting rather than another append.

The live-session banner is on and pointing at today's session. Open COBI and check it reads the way you want. Two things to know: only people on the Team & RACI roster, or anyone who has entered the team phrase, can see it — college users and the public cannot. And whoever opens the link sees where the session had got to when they clicked; they reload for anything newer. That is why it says reload rather than watch.

The Sky draws almost twice as fast as it did this morning. Open SkyView and say whether the drift reads smoothly now. If it still steps, the next lever is drawing fewer points per frame, which is what worked the last three times.

The CPL face and the light are on the map — open SkyView, press CPL and Articulations, or use the link #skyview/cpl. Two questions only you can answer: does the credential-led label read right at your zoom, and is Articulations the word you want on the button? Everything else on the face follows your eight rulings as written.

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification is the natural pilot.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. DR-24 now carries your name as its owner; say the word and the phrase gets scoped.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

Two housekeeping items behind the CPL face. Fifty-five exhibits in the articulation crosswalk are no longer in today's MAP feed; they stay on the map flagged in words rather than dropped, and the fix is a re-seed of the crosswalk from a fresh custom report. And the credit-funnel numbers the face carries for context were read by hand on 2026-09-07; refresh them after the next custom-report load.
